rationale: Both options are quantitative prefill interventions, so the persona's preference for quick, low-effort reading does not clearly favor either. Option A (truncate or replace the CoT, compare against the smoking-only control) is the more direct causal test and includes the control the context calls for. Option B (resample twenty times) is more laborious and has no control. Option A is slightly simpler in framing and addresses the question more directly, but the evidence is too thin to separate them, so the split is even.
